questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend sketching the report layout before opening the Visualizations pane in Power BI?
options: Dragging fields onto the canvas first tends to produce a report that looks assembled rather than designed, with no clear reading order
Sketching is required by Microsoft's Power BI certification exam
DAX measures cannot be created until the layout is finalized
Power BI requires a layout file to be imported before any visual can be added
questions.explain: The same discipline from planning the T-SQL query in plain English first applies to layout: deciding what each visual needs to answer before building it avoids a scattered, undesigned page.

questions.q: What are the three visuals in this report's planned layout?
options: A line chart, a pie chart, and a matrix
Four KPI cards and nothing else
A map visual, a gauge, and a scatter plot
Two KPI cards, a bar chart by territory, and a detail table
questions.explain: KPI cards answer 'how are we doing overall,' the bar chart answers 'which regions are driving sales,' and the table provides the full territory/product-line detail.

questions.q: Why does the layout avoid a line chart for this report?
options: The report covers a single quarter of data, with no series of periods to show a trend over, so a trend-over-time chart wouldn't fit the data
Line charts cannot display a Total Sales Amount measure
The stakeholder explicitly asked for only bar charts in Lesson 1
Power BI does not support line charts with grouped data
questions.explain: A line chart is built for showing change over time, but this report only has one quarter's worth of data, so there's no trend to display.

questions.q: Why does the lesson choose a flat table over a matrix for the detail visual?
options: Tables refresh faster than matrices in Import mode
Power BI matrices cannot show more than one measure at a time
A matrix cannot display both Territory and Product Line
A flat table is simpler to scan for a stakeholder and matches the row-per-combination shape the T-SQL query already produces
questions.explain: A matrix is useful for pivoting two dimensions into rows and columns, but a flat table matches the query's existing grain and is easier for a non-technical stakeholder to scan.

questions.q: What is the main reason a bar chart, rather than a pie chart, is used to show Total Sales Amount by Territory?
options: Bar charts suit comparing a small number of discrete categories; a pie chart with multiple territories and product lines would either hide detail or become unreadable
Power BI does not support pie charts on Import-mode data
Pie charts can only be used with a single measure and no dimension
Bar charts load faster than pie charts regardless of data size
questions.explain: Pie charts compare parts of a whole and get cluttered with many slices; a bar chart handles a comparison across several territories far more clearly.
